summary:
[reference generation + audio reference] A single continuous 15-second, 16:9 night demonstration. The customer's subject travels up the tall inward-curving ramp, leaves the upper lip, makes one controlled sideways righting transition, descends upright beside the ramp on pale blue-white jets, and travels away along the ground toward screen-left.

retention_analysis:
Picture roles and target times: <Picture 1> identity only, never a studio cutaway. <Picture 2> ramp-foot start at 0.00s. <Picture 3> contact with the steep ramp at 4.25s. <Picture 4> upper-lip transition at 7.25s. <Picture 5> detached, tilted righting pose with underside visible at 8.25s. <Picture 6> upright airborne descent and ground-directed jets at 9.00s. <Picture 7> ground departure at 13.25s. These are source action/composition references for one continuous shot, not literal target frames, separate shots or a slideshow. Preserve the ramp's height, inward bend, gray surface, red edge lights, ground plane, scale and camera side seen in these pictures. Keep background equipment and other background vehicles in their world positions.

detailed_description:
0.00-1.25s: establish the ramp-foot composition in Picture 2. The subject is already on the ground at the ramp approach. Map the reference stunt car's scene scale and facing direction to the customer subject without copying the car's shape.
1.25-3.25s: advance onto the bottom curve. Follow the actual ramp surface continuously, turning the subject's forward axis with the local surface tangent. For a vehicle, all appropriate wheel contacts remain coherent with the ramp.
3.25-6.50s: continue up the steep middle section, passing the exact kind of surface-contact pose in Picture 3. The ramp remains the path of travel. Do not jump from the ground to the top, cut away, reverse, teleport, or introduce a second attempt.
6.50-7.50s: follow the inward-curving upper section into Picture 4. The front extends beyond the upper lip while the rear/contact region is still close to the edge. Continue across the lip; do not hang motionless under a flat ceiling.
7.50-8.50s: separate completely from the ramp and move into the open space to screen-left. Make one continuous sideways righting transition. Pass through the tilted underside-visible pose in Picture 5 and recover the natural upright orientation. This is not an extra full barrel roll or a nose-over-tail somersault. Short blue-white jets change their visible screen direction with the tilted subject. Keep each jet root attached to the corresponding visible region on the subject; some streams are oblique during this transition.
8.50-9.25s: the subject is now approximately level and clearly airborne beside the ramp. Multiple separate narrow blue-white streams extend from its lower regions toward the ground, as in Picture 6. For a vehicle these are distributed beneath the body, with visible front/rear spacing; do not turn them into one central tail exhaust. A brief sideways stream may remain during stabilization where the reference shows it. Main downward jets are already visible before ground contact.
9.25-11.00s: descend gradually while upright. As the downward streams reach the ground, their pale cores expand into a broad white vapor cloud that spreads outward at ground level. Red venue lights tint parts of this white vapor pink. Keep roots moving with the subject and plume ends dispersing against the ground. The growing cloud progressively obscures the lower subject and contact area; do not show orange fire, black exhaust, an explosion, or instant smoke unrelated to the jet paths.
11.00-12.50s: complete the landing inside the partial vapor occlusion and continue forward. The obscured contact is not a dramatic second bounce. Do not force an unobstructed close-up of an exact impact that the references do not show.
12.50-15.00s: emerge in the same identity and travel left along the ground through the departure state in Picture 7. Leave the residual cloud behind; no continuing long rocket trail follows the departing subject.
Camera: use one coherent ground-based view. Tilt up and modestly reframe with the climb, then pan left and tilt down with the departure and descent. Let the ramp shift toward screen-right and partly leave the image. Follow the subject instead of changing to a new camera or freezing every background pixel. Keep the complete airborne action readable, natural motion blur and consistent night lighting. No captions, collage, replay, duplicate subject or model change.

summary:
[reference generation + audio reference] One continuous 15-second, 16:9 night stunt. The uploaded subject ascends the curved ramp, leaves its upper lip, rights itself once, descends upright on blue-white jets, lands and moves out of the mist. End with a clear close-up of the SAME uploaded person if the subject includes a person; otherwise finish close to the uploaded subject itself. The customer subject remains the sole stunt performer throughout.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1>: fully_preserved - same identity and structure throughout; cropping does not remove parts.
<Subject 2>: fully_preserved - specified venue only.
Pictures 2-7: attribute_transfer - successive ramp-foot, steep-contact, upper-lip, detached-righting, upright-descent and ground-departure states. Transfer no car geometry or car-mounted jet roots. Picture 7 guides ground movement, not final shot size.
<Audio 1>: reference - pacing and texture.

detailed_description:
[Shot 1: 0.00-15.00s]

0.00-1.25s: Begin near the ramp foot as in Picture 2. The customer subject approaches the curve on its own contact points. For a rider and bicycle, show the complete pair with two tires on the asphalt.

1.25-6.50s: Follow the ramp surface continuously through Picture 3's steep contact state. The subject's forward axis follows the local tangent. For a bicycle with an uploaded rider, that rider pedals; both tires follow the curve while the pair tilts together. No long braking jets.

6.50-7.50s: Follow the inward-curving upper section and pass across the lip once. The leading contact region leaves before the trailing region. For a bicycle, the front wheel leaves before the rear wheel. Do not cut, teleport or switch identity at the lip.

7.50-8.50s: Move into open air to screen-left and complete one controlled righting transition from the exit tilt to the subject's natural upright orientation. Show the same uploaded subject clearly, surrounded by empty air, with no additional object underneath. For a bicycle, retain its open frame and two wheels, plus only the rider already present in Picture 1. No reference-derived car body, underside or hidden support may appear during or after righting. Only short, oblique stabilization puffs may occur during the tilt. Do not add another full roll or somersault.

8.50-10.80s: Once upright and still airborne, descend smoothly with two separate narrow blue-white main jets directed toward the scene's GROUND PLANE. The visible streams point down, not along the direction of travel. Keep their roots attached to the same existing lower regions of the customer subject:
- Bicycle: the outer lower front fork near the front axle, and the outer lower rear frame near the rear axle. Use non-rotating frame locations; streams clear the tires.
- Person alone: beneath the two existing feet or shoe soles.
- Other subject: two separated locations on its existing underside, without adding a vehicle shell, board or support platform.
Do not emit the jets from empty space or another object. Start sustained long jets only after righting. Where they reach the ground, spread pale white vapor outward at ground level, with some pink tint from venue lights. No orange fire, black smoke or explosion.

10.80-12.00s: Land on the uploaded subject's own tires, feet or natural contact region inside partial low mist. Absorb the landing once and continue moving. Shorten and stop the main jets as contact is established. Keep the subject unchanged through the occlusion; the mist never hides or reveals an extra car.

12.00-13.00s: Emerge from the mist and move left along the ground. Show enough of the full subject to establish the completed landing and continued movement. For a rider and bicycle, clearly show the rider still riding the same bicycle on its own two tires. Leave the residual cloud behind. Begin a smooth tracking move closer from the subject's front-side quarter.

13.00-15.00s: Continue smoothly into the ending close-up.
If the uploaded subject includes a person, focus on that SAME person's visible face and upper body. Reach a head-and-shoulders close view by 14.00s and hold it clearly to the end. Match Picture 1's face, hairstyle, clothing and headwear; keep any helmet, glasses or face covering. Use a natural expression. A cyclist keeps riding, with hands or handlebars at the lower edge; the bicycle continues below the crop. No dismount, standing pose, face replacement or studio portrait.
Without a person, show the uploaded subject's recognizable front or main details closely. Invent no human face or rider.
Maintain the night venue and movement, with soft red lights and residual mist behind. Jets have stopped. No source white car may reappear underneath, behind, beside or reflected as an extra vehicle.

Camera: Tilt up with the climb, then pan left and tilt down with descent. Show the complete action until landing; then track closer from the front-side quarter. Final cropping is intentional. No hard cut, replay, duplicate, added vehicle or text.

overall_soundscape:
Use Audio 1 for continuous demonstration rhythm, jet bursts and dispersing vapor. Add no dialogue, narration or new engine roar.

summary:
[reference generation + audio reference] One continuous 15-second, 16:9 night shot. Subject 1 follows the ENTIRE ramp centerline, crosses the true upper terminal edge front-first and rear-last, clears the structure, rights itself, descends on blue-white jets and lands. Only then close in on the same uploaded person, or object if no person is present.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1>: fully_preserved - identity, structure and rider-to-mount relationship.
<Subject 2>: fully_preserved - rigid ramp and venue.
<Picture 1>: identity only. Pictures 2-7: attribute_transfer - in order, ramp-foot start, steep contact, upper terminal crossing, detached tilted righting, upright descent, ground departure. detailed_description:
[Shot 1: 0.00-15.00s, ONE uninterrupted take]

PATH AND EXIT:
The long red-lit side edges run ALONG the track; neither is the takeoff edge. The takeoff edge is the short CROSSWISE terminal edge at the very end of the upper curve, spanning the track width where both longitudinal sides terminate and the gray riding surface ends. The screen boundary is not the ramp end.
Follow the centerline; keep surface contact until each contact point reaches the terminal edge. For a bicycle, stay centered: front tire crosses the terminal edge first while the rear tire remains supported; rear tire then reaches and passes that SAME crosswise edge. Only then is the pair fully airborne. The subject never slides across a long side edge, peels off halfway around the bend or falls through the surface. No airborne roll starts while the trailing contact point is still on the ramp.

CAMERA CONTINUITY:
Use one ground-based three-quarter wide view from the source camera side. Keep camera position, focal length and roll fixed until landing. Frame the full ramp, its true top, headroom and the open landing corridor to screen-left from the start. Accept a smaller subject on the climb rather than a close-up. Keep the subject AND terminal edge visible together during approach, exit and righting. No overhead view, orbit, sudden pullback, snap zoom, cutaway or dissolve. Subject scale, position, orientation and ramp perspective remain continuous. Only after landing may the ending camera move begin.

ACTION ORDER AND APPROXIMATE PACING:
Times are approximate pacing targets. Complete each stage before the next: reach the real edge, release trailing contact, clear the structure, right the subject, then start long downward jets. If timing drifts, shorten the opening or ending hold; never skip an intermediate state or cut.

0.00-1.00s: Begin close to the ramp foot in the established wide view. The uploaded subject advances on its own tires, feet or natural contact region. No carrier underneath.

1.00-5.50s: Traverse the lower curve and steep middle continuously along the centerline. Keep forward motion and surface contact through the inward upper bend, with orientation following the surface. A steep or inverted pose does not trigger detachment. No long braking jets.

5.50-7.30s: Complete the remaining upper curve to its actual crosswise end. Show three successive states clearly: still supported just before the end; front beyond the end with the rear still supported; rear passing over that same end. Show these states in the unchanged wide view; never exit over a long side edge.

7.30-9.00s: Once fully clear, preserve forward momentum along the exit tangent before the trajectory curves naturally into the open space beside the ramp. From that SAME exit orientation, right the subject smoothly sideways, with only the pitch adjustment needed to become upright. Show every intermediate orientation: exit tilt, underside-visible tilt, partial recovery, upright. Maintain one rolling direction and the rider-mount connection. No orientation snap, position reset, extra revolution, forward somersault or replacement performer. Short stabilization puffs may follow the changing attitude; no long descent jets yet.

9.00-11.50s: Now upright and still airborne, descend with two separate narrow pale blue-white jets pointing toward the WORLD GROUND, not along travel. Use fixed existing roots: bicycle lower front fork and lower rear frame near the axles; person's existing soles; or two separated underside points of another object. Clear tires and limbs. Add no car, board, shell or spinning jet roots. As they reach the ground, spread white vapor outward, tinted pink by the red lights. No orange fire, black smoke or explosion.

11.50-12.50s: Land once inside low vapor, stop the long jets and continue left and slightly toward the camera. Establish visible ground motion on the subject's own contact points before closing in. No car emerges from the mist.

12.50-15.00s: From the same camera side, smoothly pan and optically zoom closer as the subject continues moving. No cut or camera-side reversal. With a person, finish on that same person's face and shoulders while preserving their clothes, glasses and headwear. A cyclist remains riding below the crop. Without a person, reveal the uploaded object's recognizable details; invent no face. Keep venue lights and mist behind. Shorten the ending hold if needed, never the edge crossing or righting.

overall_soundscape:
Use Audio 1 for continuous demonstration texture. Jet sounds accompany the visible puffs and braking jets. Do not force an early takeoff to hit an audio cue. No narration, dialogue or invented combustion-engine roar.

Keep the front pointing generally along the leftward path. Do not turn this into a forward somersault, multiple rolls, a flat spin, or a jump over only one invented obstacle. Their screen-space directions change with the rotating subject: the inverted phase visibly includes upward or oblique streams as well as other shorter streams. Do not force every stream to point downward throughout the roll, and do not replace all jets with one fixed rear flame. Follow Picture 5: level subject, front still toward screen-left, multiple elongated jets beneath it pointing to the ground. The streams spread into dense white vapor with red light tint near the ground. Keep the subject descending outside the parked fleet, not on a vehicle roof.
4.38-5.76s: the landing region becomes heavily obscured by vapor. Continue the same shot through the cloud; preserve the foreground lighting equipment and the true occlusion. Do not cut to a different angle or repeat the stunt to fill time.
